key_insight: This paper maps the design space of continuous diffusion language models (CDLMs), highlighting which training and architecture choices most affect performance. It focuses on two important levers—self-conditioning and embedding design—to make CDLMs more effective and better understood.
problem_solved: CDLMs are promising for fast and controllable text generation, but the field lacks a clear understanding of which design choices actually matter during training. The paper addresses this gap by studying key modeling levers that influence CDLM quality and behavior.
method: Systematically analyze self-conditioning in CDLM training to measure its effect on generation quality and stability.
Investigate embedding design choices to understand how token representation impacts continuous diffusion performance.
Compare design variants to identify practical guidelines for building stronger CDLMs.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work provides clearer guidance on how to train and tune CDLMs effectively. That can reduce guesswork, improve sampling efficiency, and help close the gap between continuous and discrete diffusion methods for language.
visual_elements: A design-space diagram showing the main CDLM training levers and their interactions
A side-by-side comparison chart of self-conditioning vs. no self-conditioning
An embedding pipeline illustration showing how tokens are mapped into continuous space
A performance heatmap summarizing which settings improve generation quality
paper_title: On the Design Space of Continuous Diffusion Language Models
paper_authors: Oscar Davis, Daan Roos, Alice Bizeul, Amitis Shidani, Victor Turrisi
